parsed.explanation: The quoted step is the sole justification of the subcase where every piece of Q is at most tau. Cut positions are arbitrary reals, so no lattice or parity constraint holds: D(Q) can take any value in [0, tau], and the claimed dichotomy D(Q) <= D(P)-1 or D(Q) >= D(P)+1 is unsupported. Reverse triangle only yields D(M) >= |D(P)-D(Q)|, which can be 0. Nothing elsewhere repairs it: the other subcase also degenerates into placeholder text ('something that forces', 'numerical checks for n<=3'), and the remark about min D over t cuts is explicitly only 'consistent with numerical data'. Hence the universal lower bound L3.3 is not established for all n; only n<=3 is claimed checked.
